section_1.title: Hook & Prerequisite Knowledge
section_1.content: Introduce the behavior of light as a wave. Review the concept of 'wave speed' in different media. Explain that light travels at its maximum speed in a vacuum (c).
section_1.example: Visualize a row of soldiers marching from a smooth pavement onto thick, muddy grass. As the soldiers hit the mud, they slow down, causing the entire line to pivot (change direction).

section_2.title: Defining Refraction & Snell's Law
section_2.content: Define refraction as the change in direction of a light wave passing from one medium to another due to a change in speed. Introduce the Refractive Index (n = c/v). Present Snell's Law: n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2).
section_2.example: A laser beam hitting a glass prism at an angle. Show an animation where the incoming angle (θ1) is compared to the outgoing angle (θ2) using a protractor overlay.

section_3.title: Visualizing the Bending Rule
section_3.content: Establish the golden rule: When light enters a denser medium (higher n), it bends toward the normal line. When entering a rarer medium, it bends away from the normal line.
section_3.example: An animation of an underwater 'Archerfish' aiming at a beetle on a branch. The fish must account for the light refracting at the water-air interface to hit its target.

section_4.title: Real-World Applications
section_4.content: Connect the theory to optical devices. Explain how convex lenses rely on refraction to converge light, forming the basis for human vision and high-tech equipment.
section_4.example: A camera lens focusing light onto a digital sensor, or a human eye showing how light bends through the cornea and lens to focus an image onto the retina.

section_5.title: Summary & Quick Check
section_5.content: Recap: Speed change leads to direction change. Final check: What happens to a straw in a glass of water? It looks 'broken' because our brain assumes light travels in straight lines.
section_5.example: A 5-second animation of a pencil being inserted into a clear glass of water, illustrating the 'broken' appearance versus the actual path of the submerged portion.

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color="#FFFFFF").to_edge(UP)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Quick Check", ["Speed changes cause refraction.", "Light bends at interfaces.", "Straws look broken underwater."])
        
        # Define elements
        straw = Line(start=UP*1.5, end=DOWN*1.5, color="#FFD700", stroke_width=8)
        water_line = Line(start=LEFT*2, end=RIGHT*2, color="#00BFFF", stroke_width=4)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#3357FF"))
        
        # Visualizing the straw
        self.place_at_grid(water_line, 'C4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(straw, 'C5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Illustrate refraction (shifted lower part)
        straw_top = Line(start=UP*1.5, end=ORIGIN, color="#FFD700", stroke_width=8)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
